scenario_text: In a decay chain, a parent nuclide decays into a radioactive daughter, which itself decays into a stable product. Both the parent and daughter populations evolve simultaneously from initial stocks. The daughter first accumulates as it is fed by the parent, then declines as its own decay dominates. The interplay of two distinct transition rates governs the buildup and decline.
